questions.question: Find a single discount (rounded up to two decimal places) equal to three consecutive discounts of 26%, 29% and 2%.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Discount for 26% and 29% = 26 + 29 − (26 × 29) ÷ 100 = 55 − 7.54 = 47.46%.

Now, combine 47.46% with 2% discount = 47.46 + 2 − (47.46 × 2) ÷ 100.

⇒ 49.46 − 0.9492 = 48.5108%.

Rounding up to two decimal places, we get 48.51%.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.51%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Three consecutive discounts: **d₁ = 26%**, **d₂ = 29%**, and **d₃ = 2%**.
Formulas: **Net SP = MP × (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)% × (100 − d₃)%** | **Single Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2277b99a546dc882c8125320e856fc498fd750504a65e48867d9fd7136e14c5.png] 
⇒ Let the **Marked Price (MP)** be 100.
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 100 × (74 ÷ 100) × (71 ÷ 100) × (98 ÷ 100).
⇒ SP = 100 × 0.74 × 0.71 × 0.98 = 51.4892.
⇒ **Single Equivalent Discount** = MP − SP = 100 − 51.4892 = 48.5108%.
⇒ Rounded to two decimal places = 48.51%.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.51%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two or more discounts are applied one after another, they are called **successive discounts**. The total effective discount is always less than the simple sum of individual discounts.

Formula for Two Discounts

For two discounts a% and b%, the **Single Equivalent Discount** = [a + b − (ab ÷ 100)]%.</p

questions.question: A seller marks their goods 45% above the cost price. On customer demand, they offer a 60% reduction on the bills. What percentage of profit or loss does the seller make?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, markup percentage **a = +45%** and discount percentage **b = −60%**.

Net change = 45 − 60 + (45 × (−60)) ÷ 100

Net change = −15 − 2700 ÷ 100 = −15 − 27 = **−42%**.

The negative sign indicates a **loss of 42%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 42% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup = 45% above CP, Discount = 60% on MP.
**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Loss% = (CP − SP) ÷ CP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0a07e0c8738a54dbf19295fec919a1a7c05355cd98b9f5d1c5cf449c6580bbd.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 45% of 100 = 145.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = MP − 60% of MP = 145 × (40 ÷ 100) = 58.

⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 58 = 42.

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = (42 ÷ 100) × 100 = 42%.

**∴ The correct answer is 42% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Marked price is the price printed on an article. Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price** to arrive at the Selling Price.

Net Profit or Loss

The final profit or loss depends on the cumulative effect of the initial **markup** and the subsequent **discount** offered.</p

Let the **cost of production** be x.

Successive selling: x × (110 ÷ 100) × (115 ÷ 100) × (125 ÷ 100) = 31,900.

Using multiplier: x × 1.1 × 1.15 × 1.25 = 31,900.

x = 31,900 ÷ (1.1 × 1.15 × 1.25) ≈ 20,173.91.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20,174.**

⇒ P × (11 ÷ 10) × (23 ÷ 20) × (5 ÷ 4) = 31,900.
⇒ P × (1265 ÷ 800) = 31,900.

Chain of Profit

When a product passes through multiple hands, the final price is the result of **successive percentage increases** on the initial cost.

questions.question: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 50% above its cost price. What percentage of discount on the marked price should be allowed to gain 14%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100 units.

**Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150 units.

Desired **Selling Price (SP)** for 14% gain = 100 + 14 = 114 units.

**Discount** to be allowed = MP − SP = 150 − 114 = 36 units.

**Discount%** = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (36 ÷ 150) × 100 = 24%.

**∴ The correct answer is 24%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup% = 50%, Gain% = 14%.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 | MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/75d9273710c7f4aa18a50d30ca09dc1c7268be9a3e4cecdcb767117d55d3f818.png] 

⇒ Assume **Cost Price** = 100.

⇒ **Marked Price** = 100 × (150 ÷ 100) = 150.

⇒ **Selling Price** for 14% profit = 100 × (114 ÷ 100) = 114.

⇒ **Discount** = MP − SP = 150 − 114 = 36.

⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (36 ÷ 150) × 100 = 24%.

**∴ The correct answer is 24%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The price listed on the label is the **Marked Price**. Discount is always calculated on this value to reach the final **Selling Price**.

Relation Formula

MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%). This ratio can directly solve for missing variables in markup/discount problems.</p

questions.question: If the selling price of a bed is 2-times of initial, then the profit is 6-times of initial. Find the initial profit percentage (in %).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let initial **Selling Price (SP)** be 100 and **Profit** be P. New SP = 200 and New Profit = 6P.

Profit difference = (200 − 100) = 100.

In terms of P, Profit difference = 6P − P = 5P.

5P = 100 ⇒ P = 20. Initial CP = SP − P = 100 − 20 = 80.

Profit% = (20 ÷ 80) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** New SP = 2 × Initial SP, New Profit = 6 × Initial Profit.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5996563b3e52267aa9891f6cfdc7cf9e2ffa9cea885503672fc467463987669d.png] 

⇒ Let initial **Cost Price** be CP and initial **Selling Price** be SP.

⇒ Initial Profit (P) = SP − CP.

⇒ New Selling Price = 2SP. New Profit = 2SP − CP.

⇒ According to question: 2SP − CP = 6(SP − CP).

⇒ 2SP − CP = 6SP − 6CP ⇒ 5CP = 4SP ⇒ SP = 1.25CP.

⇒ Profit = 1.25CP − CP = 0.25CP.

⇒ Profit% = (0.25CP ÷ CP) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relationship between SP and Profit

When CP remains constant, any increase in **Selling Price** directly adds to the **Profit** amount. The change in profit is equal to the change in selling price.

Profit Percentage

Profit% is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless otherwise specified in the problem statement.</p

questions.question: Find the effective price percentage of the marked price after three consecutive discounts of 8%, 16% and 3%. (Rounded up to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective price percentage = (100 − d₁)% × (100 − d₂)% × (100 − d₃)%

Effective price = 100 × (92/100) × (84/100) × (97/100)

Effective price = 0.92 × 0.84 × 97% = 0.7728 × 97%

Effective price = 74.9616% ≈ 74.96%

**∴ The correct answer is 74.96%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Three consecutive discounts of **8%**, **16%**, and **3%**.

**Formulas:** Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100 × (100 − d₃)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9cb129b2f8b43086d25c305a0159454795c5f017ea3c6d25c44a6be947a91084.png] 

⇒ Let the **Marked Price** be 100 units.

⇒ Price after 8% discount = 100 − 8 = 92 units.

⇒ Price after 16% discount = 92 − (16% of 92) = 92 − 14.72 = 77.28 units.

⇒ Price after 3% discount = 77.28 − (3% of 77.28) = 77.28 − 2.3184 = 74.9616 units.

⇒ **Effective Price Percentage** = (74.9616/100) × 100 ≈ 74.96%.

**∴ The correct answer is 74.96%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Discount Rate

To find the total discount, use the formula for successive discounts: a + b − (ab/100). Subtracting this from 100 gives the final price.

Relationship between MP and SP

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (1 − Discount%/100). The effective price percentage is essentially the ratio of SP to MP expressed as a percentage.</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 52% above its cost price. What percentage of discount on the marked price should be allowed to gain 14%?

100 − D = 75 ⇒ **D = 25%**.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys 20 pens at ₹15 each and another 30 pens at ₹10 each. He mixes all the pens and sells them at ₹14 each. What is the profit or loss per pen he makes on an average?

Total pens = 20 + 30 = 50 pens.

Weighted Average CP = (20 × 15 + 30 × 10) ÷ 50.

Average CP = (300 + 300) ÷ 50 = 600 ÷ 50 = ₹12 per pen.

Selling Price (SP) = ₹14 per pen.

Profit per pen = SP − CP = 14 − 12 = ₹2.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2 profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Quantity 1** = 20, **Rate 1** = ₹15; **Quantity 2** = 30, **Rate 2** = ₹10; **SP** = ₹14.
Formulas: Total CP = (Q₁ × C₁) + (Q₂ × C₂) | Average CP = Total CP ÷ Total Quantity | Profit = SP − CP
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d50df1d70232f0949aaa3dd56b031829802b7cc31427045888b5930033b7ffb.png] 
⇒ Total CP = (20 × 15) + (30 × 10) = 300 + 300 = ₹600.
⇒ Total Quantity = 20 + 30 = 50 pens.
⇒ Average CP per pen = 600 ÷ 50 = ₹12.
⇒ Selling Price per pen = ₹14.
⇒ Profit per pen = 14 − 12 = ₹2.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2 profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Cost

When items of different prices are mixed, the average cost price is calculated by dividing the total cost of all items by the total quantity.

Profit and Loss

If Selling Price (SP) > Cost Price (CP), it is a Profit. Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.question: The selling price of 30 books is equal to the cost price of 36 books. Find the loss or gain percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Selling Price (SP)** to **Cost Price (CP)** can be derived from the given condition.

30 × SP = 36 × CP ⇒ SP ÷ CP = 36 ÷ 30 = 6 ÷ 5.

Profit ratio units = 6 − 5 = 1 unit.

Gain% = (Profit units ÷ CP units) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

Since SP > CP, it is a **gain**.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Selling price of 30 books = Cost price of 36 books.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02bac884745f355d98118adb92c3afc69a908b8152c93f984bb7412430978add.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 book be Re. 1.

⇒ CP of 36 books = Rs. 36.

⇒ According to the question, SP of 30 books = CP of 36 books = Rs. 36.

⇒ CP of 30 books = Rs. 30.

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 36 − 30 = Rs. 6.

⇒ Profit% = (6 ÷ 30) × 100 = 1/5 × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss on Quantity

When the CP of 'm' articles is equal to the SP of 'n' articles, the **gain or loss percentage** is given by [(m − n) ÷ n] × 100. A positive result indicates gain, and a negative result indicates loss.

Cost Price & Selling Price Relationship

If the number of items sold is **less** than the number of items bought for the same price, there is always a **gain**.</p

questions.question: An article is sold for ₹x. If it is sold at 25% of this price, there is a loss of 50%. What is the percentage profit when it is sold for ₹x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **original selling price** x = 100.

New selling price = 25% of 100 = 25.

Given, at SP = 25, there is a **loss of 50%**. ∴ CP × 50/100 = 25 ⇒ CP = 50.

Profit at original SP = Original SP − CP = 100 − 50 = 50.

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (50 ÷ 50) × 100 = 100%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Selling Price = x; New SP = 0.25x; Loss% = 50%.

**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%); Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2ff800b71a821e26667df1af493f5b8c08c982ca0a08fa1ccae66dc27a84977.png] 

⇒ Let original SP = x.

⇒ Case 2: SP = 0.25x. Loss = 50%.

⇒ CP = (0.25x × 100) ÷ (100 − 50) = 25x ÷ 50 = 0.5x.

⇒ When sold at original SP (x): Profit = x − 0.5x = 0.5x.

⇒ Profit% = (0.5x ÷ 0.5x) × 100 = 100%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price & Selling Price Relationship

If SP > CP, it is a **Profit**. If CP > SP, it is a **Loss**. Profit/Loss% is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise.

Multiplier Method

A loss of 50% means SP is 0.5 times the CP. A profit of 100% means SP is 2 times the CP.</p

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Marked Price & Selling Price

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.</p

questions.question: A man sold an article at a gain of 57%. If he had sold it for ₹238 more, he would have gained 82%. The cost price (in ₹) of the article is:

Profit and Loss on Cost Price
